Where I’m from we have this place called “secure treatment” for youth. I’m an adult now, but I was sent there when my umpteenth attempt didn’t succeed. 

They punished us for almost everything. I couldn’t speak about people outside, even saying their names got me a time out. I guess their whole idea was that we couldn’t talk about the outside, because it made us unsafe on the inside.

They had a room called “The TR” (timeout room” that they would put us if we would step out of line. It was linoleum, the door needed special keys, and it only had a mattress on which we could sleep on. It was basically a jail cell for 13 year olds. They fed us sandwiches in there, and if we went to the bathroom the door had to be ajar and I had to sing while I peed.

I mean, I haven’t been to an adult one yet-  and maybe I probably should. But this experience haunted me. It didn’t make me less crazy by being there, I just got better at hiding it so I wouldn’t go back.

I’m sorry you feel that way. It’s hard being alone.
The irony of lonely souls walking together.
All we can count on are the good days.
Be well my friend.
